Taos Pueblo

Taos Pueblo is a living Tiwa-speaking Pueblo community in northern New Mexico. Pueblo-published accounts of Blue Lake and community-directed language education provide two different ways to begin: a history of land recovery and a record of teaching across generations.

03

Blue Lake and a public history of land recovery

The Pueblo’s account identifies December 15, 1970 as the date of the Blue Lake return and places that event within a longer struggle for self-determination. This public historical account is a starting point for understanding the community’s land recovery; it does not provide permission to visit restricted places or establish present legal boundaries.

Read the sources [4] Taos Pueblo

04

Tiwa teaching across generations

The Department of Education describes school partnerships, adult classes and instructor development. Its account names school milestones in 2019, 2021 and 2022 and reports a transition to online adult classes in 2020. These are the programme’s reported activities, rather than an independent measure of language proficiency or a promise that particular classes are currently offered.

Read the sources [5] Taos Pueblo Department of Education

Blue Lake — Pueblo account of the 1970 land return ↗

The Pueblo places the December 1970 Blue Lake return within its public account of self-determination and a long effort to recover land taken in the early twentieth century.
